messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — High GPU queue growth detected in us-east-1 (gpu-pool-v2). Autoscaler not increasing instances. Custom metrics backend showing delayed responses. dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/gpu-ops

jess: ack oncall, looking. Confirming increased queue length and rising 429s from inference-proxy. pinging infra.

jess: quick query: ```promql
sum(rate(gpu_queue_length_total[1m])) by (pool)
``` returns big spike for gpu-pool-v2 (x8 higher than baseline).

akira: seeing lots of 5xx from metrics-adapter to prometheus over last 10m. snippets from adapter logs: ```ERROR fetchCustomMetric: read tcp 10.1.2.3:443: connection reset by peer
ERROR handler failed to convert metrics: timeout```. Likely backlog/backpressure to adapter.

rafa: if adapter is failing HPAs that rely on custom metrics will not scale. can you `kubectl get pods -n redwood-metrics` and check restarts?

jess: running quick checks — metrics-adapter-7c9b8 restarted 24 times in last hour, metrics-server stable. Looks like adapter OOM or connection resets.

jess: attempt mitigation: rolling restart adapter to clear connections and drop backlog — ```kubectl rollout restart deployment/metrics-adapter -n redwood-metrics```

infra-bot: deploy pipeline: redeploy/metrics-adapter triggered by jess. CI job 5643 started.

jess: adapter pods came back up but HPA events still show "failed to get metric" for custom/gpu_queue. HPA events: ```Warning FailedGetExternalMetric 3m (x4 over 5m) failed to get external metric gpu_queue: 500 internal error```

kevin: what's the customer impact? are any tenants seeing errors?

jess: short answer: yes — customers on GPU pools in us-east-1 seeing elevated latencies and token throttling. 3 customers showing 10-20% error increase, one has timed-out batches. Seen spike in 429s at proxy and backlog growth in queue. posting quick status to status.redwood.ai — will update.

maria: flagging to account team, prepping short note for impacted customers: "We detected elevated inference errors and queueing in us-east-1; working on mitigation, scaling and metrics recovery in progress."

akira: metrics-adapter logs still show degraded connectivity to prometheus; suspect scrape cardinality increased (new per-tenant label) causing high memory usage. check pod memory.

jess: memory graphs show adapter at 1.9Gi (limit 2Gi) and climbing. OOM risk. I can bump temporarily or manually scale GPU pool to relieve immediate customer latency while we stabilize metrics. Thoughts?

rafa: manual scale to buy time. Autoscaler is useless until adapter stops returning metrics. Do manual pool scale: ```redwood-scalectl increase --pool gpu-pool-v2 --count 8 --reason "incident 3172501234 manual scale"``` — then monitor queue drain.

jess: executed manual scale command, controller shows 8 nodes added, provisioning in progress (ETA ~3m).

infra-bot: cloud-provider: started provisioning 8 gpu instances for pool gpu-pool-v2 (request id cp-8932).

rafa: after nodes join, queue length started decreasing but observed ~3-4m delay before HPA recognized metrics even after adapter restart. That explains why autoscale lagged.

kevin: ok — immediate mitigation worked. what's next for full remediation and RCA?

jess: short-term followups: 1) increase adapter memory limit to 3Gi in staging and promote config, 2) add liveness/readiness probes to fail fast on stuck connections, 3) add circuit breaker between adapter and prometheus to avoid OOM from cardinality storms, 4) add alert for adapter restart rate.

akira: will collect heap profile from adapter for post-incident analysis. schedule: taking heap dump now (will attach link in ticket).

rafa: taking incident owner for next shift. I'm doing a formal incident doc and will open INC-2026-4321 with timeline, mitigations, and customer impact.

jess: oncall handoff to rafa at 3172501300 UTC — summary: cause likely adapter overload from high cardinality scrapes -> adapter started restarting -> HPAs lost custom metrics -> autoscaler didn’t scale -> GPU pool exhausted leading to queue growth and throttling. Mitigations taken: restarted adapter, manual pool scale +8, posting status. Next steps for SRE/infra: follow jess list + prod deploy of adapter memory bump + probe changes.

rafa: ack taking over, I'll coordinate with platform to temp increase adapter mem limit, and follow up on long-term fixes. Setting priority P2 for customer impact and scheduling postmortem.

kevin: thanks everyone — please keep status updates in INC-2026-4321 and paste any customer-facing text here before posting. :thumbsup:

maria: I'll send the customer note now and coordinate ongoing comms.
